_problem: feature_session_management_tech.md:120 (Capacity × visibility, PRD E#7 authority) pins that visibility='public' requires slots_max IS NOT NULL and fail-closes at the SessionService choke-point on create and on every update reaching public. It then states that a row which is public + slots_max IS NULL existing OUTSIDE that choke-point (legacy, fixture, or writer bypass — the DB column stays nullable, there is no CHECK) is an invalid state that MUST NOT appear in the public discovery projection, and it explicitly DELEGATES the concrete handling (skip/reject + audit) and the regression test to feature_marketplace_discovery_tech.md as the owner of public projection. That delegation has never been executed: grep shows slots_max appears ZERO times in the marketplace BE spec today. So the invariant is asserted in one document and owned by another that does not mention it — a projector built from the marketplace spec alone would not know to guard it.
_decision_contract: This slice does NOT re-open the product decision (that a public + NULL row must never surface publicly) — that is already owner-pinned via PRD E#7 and feature_session_management_tech §2. It executes the delegated TECHNICAL choice, which session_management explicitly assigned to the discovery owner: the projector SKIPS the offending row (does not upsert; deletes any pre-existing projection of it), emits an integrity audit signal identifying the session, and CONTINUES the batch. Rationale for skip-and-continue over reject-and-halt: the invariant to protect is 'this row never surfaces', which skipping already satisfies; halting the projector on one legacy row would convert a single-row data-integrity fault into a full marketplace discovery outage, i.e. fail-closed on the row is correct, fail-closed on the whole surface is a self-inflicted availability incident. The audit signal is what prevents silent tolerance.
